name: Compressing and Reusing Data Efficiently
gist: Papers figure out how to build smaller datasets that still teach models the important things, or how to turn larger datasets into more useful versions without losing information.
explain: Building datasets is expensive and time-consuming. Collecting millions of examples, labeling them, cleaning them costs enormous effort. So researchers in this subtheme ask: can you accomplish the same goal with fewer examples? Can you take a large, messy dataset and distill it into something smaller and cleaner that teaches a model the same essential things? Can you take a dataset built for one purpose and reformat it so it works for another? The goal is to get more learning value from less data.

Why does this matter? Training a large AI model on a huge dataset is expensive—it costs time and electricity. If you can achieve similar learning with less data, you save time and money because you need fewer computers running for fewer hours, and you can try new ideas faster because each experiment finishes sooner. Also, sometimes you have access to relevant data but in the wrong format or mixed with lots of noise. If you can transform or compress it smartly, you unlock data that would otherwise be useless. The challenge is that you cannot just randomly throw data away or simplify it—if you lose important examples, the model will learn less. You have to understand which examples matter and which are redundant or harmful.

The papers here take different approaches. Some use machine learning itself to identify which examples are most valuable for training, then remove the rest. Others use data distillation: run a learning process that compresses a large dataset into a much smaller but representative synthetic dataset that teaches almost as much. Still others focus on data cleaning: taking a messy dataset and keeping only the high-quality examples, or fixing mislabeled data. The work matters because it makes AI training faster and cheaper, and gets more value from data that already exists.

papers.title: Benchmarking Bias Mitigation Toward Fairness Without Harm from Vision to LVLMs
papers.contribution: Shows that many debiasing methods don't reliably outperform well-tuned ERM baseline, while composite data-augmentation consistently delivers parity gains without sacrificing utility.

papers.title: COMPACT: COMPositional Atomic-to-Complex Visual Capability Tuning
papers.contribution: Reduces VIT data budget by 90% while achieving 100.2% of full VIT performance and improves performance on complex benchmarks like MM-Vet (+8.6%) and MMStar (+2.9%).

papers.title: Common Corpus: The Largest Collection of Ethical Data for LLM Pre-Training
papers.contribution: Contains approximately two trillion tokens with wide language coverage from high-resource European languages to underrepresented low-resource languages, plus significant code data.

papers.title: Dataset Distillation as Pushforward Optimal Quantization
papers.contribution: DDOQ achieves SOTA performance on ImageNet-1K higher per-class settings, with better inter-model generalization than clustering method D4M, first demonstrating consistency of distilled datasets for diffusion priors.

papers.title: Demystifying Supervision Data Generalization in Multimodal LMs
papers.contribution: Correlates 86.0% with actual performance rankings and achieves up to 6.9% improvement in average accuracy over uniform selection of supervision datasets.

papers.title: Do We Need All the Synthetic Data? Targeted Image Augmentation via Diffusion Models
papers.contribution: By augmenting only 30%-40% of data, achieves up to 2.8% generalization improvement across various architectures and optimizers, including surpassing SAM with SGD on CIFAR-100.

papers.title: Nemotron-CC-Math: A 133 Billion-Token-Scale High Quality Math Pretraining Dataset
papers.contribution: Nemotron-CC-Math-4+ surpasses prior open datasets with 5.5x more tokens than FineMath-4+, yielding +4.8 to +12.6 gains on MATH and +4.6 to +14.3 on MBPP+.

papers.title: When Large Multimodal Models Confront Evolving Knowledge: Challenges and Explorations
papers.contribution: Reveals that knowledge-aware augmentation strengthens injection performance and MoE/Data Replay methods mitigate capability degradation across 9,422 samples in 159 subtypes.

papers.title: CHAMMI-75: pre-training multi-channel models with heterogeneous microscopy images
papers.contribution: Training with CHAMMI-75 improves performance on multi-channel bioimaging tasks, enabling next-generation cellular morphology models.

papers.title: ClarifyVC: Clarifying Ambiguous Commands in Vehicle Control with a Hybrid Data Augmentation Pipeline
papers.contribution: Achieves 15% higher parsing accuracy, 20% stronger ambiguity resolution, and 98% protocol compliance on realistic in-cabin scenarios.

papers.title: DIVER: Diving Deeper into Distilled Data via Expressive Semantic Recovery
papers.contribution: DIVER significantly improves cross-architecture generalization of distilled data while requiring processing time comparable to raw DiT on ImageNet (256×256) with only 4 GB GPU memory.

papers.title: Evaluating Sample Utility for Efficient Data Selection by Mimicking Model Weights
papers.contribution: Mimic scores guide training to improve data efficiency and accelerate convergence with consistent gains across six image datasets; CLIP models trained with 4.7M fewer samples show improved performance.

papers.title: Evaluating Text Creativity across Diverse Domains: a Dataset and Large Language Model Evaluator
papers.contribution: CrEval demonstrates superior alignment with human judgments over existing methods and shows that integrating both human-generated and synthetic data yields robust evaluators.

papers.title: From Medical Records to Diagnostic Dialogues: A Clinical-Grounded Approach and Dataset for Psychiatric Comorbidity
papers.contribution: Construct PsyCoTalk, the first large-scale 3,000-dialogue comorbidity dataset with high structural and linguistic fidelity and confirmed diagnostic validity.

papers.title: Grounding and Enhancing Informativeness and Utility in Dataset Distillation
papers.contribution: Achieves 6.1% performance improvement over prior state-of-the-art on ImageNet-1K with ResNet-18.

papers.title: Hard Labels In! Rethinking the Role of Hard Labels in Mitigating Local Semantic Drift
papers.contribution: Achieves 42.7% ImageNet-1K accuracy with only 285M soft-label storage (100x reduction) outperforming LPLD by 9.0%.

papers.title: InfoDet: A Dataset for Infographic Element Detection
papers.contribution: InfoDet enables development of accurate object detection for charts/HROs; applications include Thinking-with-Boxes scheme for VLM chart understanding and document layout detection.

papers.title: Is Data Shapley Not Better than Random in Data Selection? Ask NASH
papers.contribution: NASH substantially improves the effectiveness of Shapley-based data selection with minimal computational overhead by identifying and exploiting Shapley-informative components.

papers.title: Is Graph Mixup Beneficial? Investigating Interpolation And Empirical Performance of Graph Mixup Methods
papers.contribution: Finds that state-of-the-art mixup methods yield no statistically significant improvements over no-mixup baselines and that high interpolation error leads to performance degradation.

papers.title: Memory-Distilled Selection for Noise-Robust Anomaly Detection
papers.contribution: Achieves 99.16% image-level AUROC on MVTecAD at 40% noise ratio and state-of-the-art on VisA and Real-IAD under noisy conditions without hyperparameter tuning.

papers.title: PICABench: How Far are We from Physical Realistic Image Editing?
papers.contribution: Evaluation of mainstream models reveals physical realism remains challenging with large room to explore; PICA-100K dataset enables learning physics from videos.

papers.title: PluRel: Synthetic Data unlocks Scaling Laws for Relational Foundation Models
papers.contribution: First demonstration that RFM pretraining loss exhibits power-law scaling with synthetic databases; synthetic pretraining provides strong base for real database fine-tuning.

papers.title: Principled Synthetic Data Enables the First Scaling Laws for LLMs in Recommendation
papers.contribution: Synthetic data models outperform real data models by 130% on recall@100; establishes first robust power-law scaling for continual pre-trained LLMs in recommendations.

papers.title: ProtoVAR: Efficient Dataset Distillation via Prototype-Guided Visual Autoregressive Modeling
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art distillation performance with comparable or lower computational cost than diffusion-based approaches.

papers.title: Rectified Decoupled Dataset Distillation: A Closer Look for Fair and Comprehensive Evaluation
papers.contribution: Analysis reveals much performance variation stems from inconsistent evaluation rather than synthetic data quality differences, and identifies strategies that improve distilled dataset effectiveness.

papers.title: Relational In-Context Learning via Synthetic Pre-training with Structural Prior
papers.contribution: RDB-PFN achieves strong few-shot performance on 19 real-world relational prediction tasks, outperforming state-of-the-art tabular foundation models with lightweight architecture and fast inference.

papers.title: RoboCasa365: A Large-Scale Simulation Framework for Training and Benchmarking Generalist Robots
papers.contribution: Extensive experiments reveal how task diversity, dataset scale, and environment variation shape generalist robot generalization and inform future progress strategies.

papers.title: S2R-HDR: A Large-Scale Rendered Dataset for HDR Fusion
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art HDR fusion performance on real-world datasets, bridging synthetic-to-real domain gap.

papers.title: Scalable RF Simulation in Generative 4D Worlds
papers.contribution: Simulated signals show high fidelity on phase-sensitive benchmarks and improve downstream RF imaging and activity recognition tasks with gains that grow with data volume.

papers.title: THEMIS: Towards Holistic Evaluation of MLLMs for Scientific Paper Fraud Forensics
papers.contribution: Even the best-performing model falls below passing threshold, demonstrating THEMIS presents a stringent test for complex, real-world fraud detection tasks.

papers.title: Training Data Efficiency in Multimodal Process Reward Models
papers.contribution: BIS-selected subsets reach full-data performance using only 10% of training data on InternVL2.5-8B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B, improving over random subsampling by 4.1% relative.

papers.title: When Data is the Algorithm: A Systematic Study and Curation of Preference Optimization Datasets
papers.contribution: Reveals structural and qualitative discrepancies in reward margins; curates UltraMix 30% smaller than best individual dataset while exceeding performance across key benchmarks.
